newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian parliament backs new finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Latvian parliament backs new finance minister.

text.p: Latvia's parliament on Thursday backed the appointment of Vassily Melnik as the country's new finance minister, the parliament press office said.
Melnik, 29, gained the support of 44 MPs with 24 against. A total 71 MPs of the 100-seat parliament were present, the press parliament press service said in a statement.

Melnik''s appointment had caused some controversy after a newspaper said he was being investigated for a conflict of interests. The prosecutor's office later confirmed the report but said that it had found no breach of anti-corruption laws.
Latvia has been without a finance minister since October, when the previous one was sacked.
Prime Minister Andris Shkele was acting prime minister and during this time took the controversial deficit-free 1997 budget through parliament.
Melnik is part of the largest party in the six-party coalition government, the Democratic Party Saimnieks.

He is also involved in several companies, including a ship repair company, a board member of Latvian Gas and the deputy chairman of the board of the Latvian Shipping Company, one of the Baltic state's largest firms.

As finance minister, Melnik will be responsible for making sure the government fulfills the balanced budget, which came after a near 40 million lat deficit in 1996 and a 90 million lat funding gap in 1995.
The balanced 1997 budget is part of Latvia's commitments to the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in return for IMF credits.
